rationale: Registry of canonical path strings (filesystem paths, package paths, executable arguments). When a path is renamed/moved, add the deprecated form to this registry so path-canonical-ripple.ts flags every surviving occurrence in the configured scope. Keep entries focused on string forms that machines verify; semantic recasts (e.g. Tier-8-vs-Tier-1 framing changes) belong in the failure-mode catalog audit layer instead.

paths.note: Plan-023 Tier 1 partial substrate carve-out collapsed shell/renderer into a single apps/desktop workspace. Deprecated forms are written without the trailing slash on purpose — `git grep -F` is a substring match, so `apps/desktop/shell` catches BOTH the literal-path form (`apps/desktop/shell/foo.ts`) AND the executable / CLI form (`pnpm rebuild --filter=apps/desktop/shell better-sqlite3`); the latter is the form that escaped the original PR #24 review per failure-mode-catalog.md row CAT-01. docs/archive/** retains historical references; docs/operations/failure-mode-catalog.md documents the failure pattern itself and must contain the literal deprecated string.

Plan-007 owns the bin map; its 2026-08-25 Decision Log canonicalized the CLI executable to `sidekicks` and repaired Spec-026's drifted deep-link scheme spelling to the `sidekicks://` value Spec-023 already made canonical. ONLY the invocation name and that one drifted scheme spelling moved — the npm package scope (@ai-sidekicks/*), the repo name, the config directories, the keystore key prefix (ai-sidekicks:*), the PASETO iss/aud claims, the ai-sidekicks-schema workflow marker, the daemon serviceName, and the winget package id are all deliberately unchanged. MATCHER: regex, not literal. The bare project name survives on all those surfaces, so a bare needle is unusable, and a fixed-string needle spelling `<executable> <verb>` is imprecise in BOTH directions — it misses whitespace variants (space runs, tabs) and, having no trailing boundary, it fires on project-name prose continuing into a longer word (a `config` verb inside 'configuration', a `run` verb inside 'running'). Both directions were observed, not theorized: the over-match direction failed CI on this entry's own PR, where a hyphen-suffixed fixed-string needle matched `--repository <owner>/ai-sidekicks --environment production` in docs/backlog.md — legitimate, deliberately-unchanged prose. The prefix guard is what excludes it. THE GUARD IS ONE SHARED ALTERNATION, spelled once and reused by every invocation needle, and it has two arms. The plain arm `(^|[^[:alnum:]@/_-])` rejects a preceding `/` (repo slug), `@` (npm scope), and word characters. The path arm readmits exactly the slash the plain arm rejects, but only behind a FILESYSTEM-PATH ANCHOR — an optional run of `.` or `~`, then a slash — so `/usr/local/bin/ai-sidekicks`, `./ai-sidekicks`, `../tools/ai-sidekicks` and `~/bin/ai-sidekicks` are all seen while `<owner>/ai-sidekicks` is not. **That arm's own leading boundary is an ENUMERATION, not an exclusion, and the difference is load-bearing.** It lists what may precede a path — start of line, whitespace, a quote, a backtick, an open paren, `=`, `[` — rather than subtracting what may not. The subtractive spelling was tried first and failed on this corpus's own prose: written as "any character that is not a word character, `@`, `.`, `/`, `:` or `-`", the `>` closing a `<owner>/` placeholder satisfied it, so `--repository <owner>/ai-sidekicks --environment production` — a package-registry command in docs/backlog.md, and the exact prose that had already failed CI once on this entry — became a hit again, along with the `<path>/…` placeholders this note and the §6 entry use to DESCRIBE the gate. An exclusion list has to anticipate every punctuation mark a future author might put before a slash; an enumeration only has to cover the ways a real path is actually introduced. The enumeration also excludes `:` implicitly, which is what keeps a URL out: `https://github.com/owner/ai-sidekicks run history` would otherwise satisfy the path arm through the `//` after the scheme. This shared-alternation shape is a repair with a review round behind it — the guard was first written as a SEPARATE path-anchored needle carrying its own copy of the verb alternation, which covered `<path>/ai-sidekicks <verb>` and silently left `<path>/ai-sidekicks --help` and `<path>/ai-sidekicks \\` uncovered, because those two signatures lived on needles the path arm had never been added to. A guard that is per-signature is a guard that decays per-signature; sharing one alternation makes the coverage a property of the guard rather than of whoever remembered to copy it. ERE ONLY — no \b and no lookaround: `git grep -E` compiles through the platform's regex engine and the GNU extensions are not portable across the CI matrix, so boundaries are spelled as POSIX character classes. THE SIX NEEDLES — needles (1), (2), (5) and (6) all carry the shared two-arm guard above, so each sees both the bare and the path-qualified spelling of its signature: (1) executable followed by any first-level command verb, whitespace-tolerant and boundary-guarded at both ends — the verb alternation enumerates every verb the corpus currently spells, not only the eight the 2026-08-25 sweep rewrote, so a regression on an already-defined group (workflow, onboarding, db, cp, ...) is caught too; extend it when a new first-level verb joins the CLI surface. (2) The root/global-flag invocations that carry no verb (`--help`, `--version`, `-h`, flag-first forms like `--no-banner daemon status`), since a hyphen cannot start a verb. (3) The bin-map KEY, matched independently of JSON colon spacing — JSON permits whitespace between a property name and its colon, so `{"bin":{"ai-sidekicks" : "./dist/main.js"}}` is a valid manifest that would install the deprecated executable; the needle is key-position-anchored (closing quote plus optional whitespace plus colon) so it never matches a VALUE — load-bearing, because the project name is deliberately unchanged and legitimately appears as a value (`"name": "ai-sidekicks"` in the root package.json) and this entry's scope includes docs/**/*.md. The needle additionally requires the value to OPEN WITH A QUOTE, which is a narrowing rather than a decoration: key position alone fires on any object keyed by the deliberately-unchanged project name — `const repositories = { "ai-sidekicks": config }` in a source file, `{"ai-sidekicks": {"version": "1.0"}}` in a documented config example, `{ "ai-sidekicks": ["apps/*"] }` in a workspace map — none of which is a `bin` entry, and all of which are legitimate in this entry's scope. Requiring a string value removes that whole class while keeping every real form, INCLUDING the multi-line manifest (`"bin": {` on one line, the key on the next), which no single-line construct anchor could reach. The surviving residual is narrow and named: a string-valued key that is not a `bin` entry (a dependency-style `{"ai-sidekicks": "^1.0.0"}`) still matches. That is accepted — a dependency on the workspace root's own name is not a form this corpus writes, and tightening further (demanding a path-shaped value) would guess at `bin` values npm does not constrain. (4) The unquoted prose shorthand plans use when restating the map, whitespace-tolerant. (5) The deep-link scheme, boundary-guarded so the `ai-sidekicks:` keystore key prefix is not matched. (6) The executable ending a line with a shell line-continuation backslash. This one exists because `git grep` is LINE-ORIENTED — it evaluates one line at a time, so `[[:space:]]+` in needle (1) can never consume a newline and a two-line invocation escapes it entirely. Needle (6) closes that by matching the continuation SIGNATURE rather than the invocation: the executable, REQUIRED trailing whitespace, a backslash, end of line. It deliberately does not look at the next line, and it does not need to. The whitespace is required rather than optional, and that is a repair with a counterexample behind it: written `[[:space:]]*`, the needle also matched a Windows configuration path ending in the directory `%APPDATA%\ai-sidekicks\` — the preceding backslash satisfies the prefix guard, zero whitespace satisfies the quantifier, and the directory separator satisfies the trailing backslash — so it flagged a config directory this same note lists as deliberately unchanged. Demanding at least one space or tab separates the shell form (`ai-sidekicks \`) from the path form (`...\ai-sidekicks\`) and costs only the zero-space continuation, which no author writes. Prose ending in the bare name still does not match, for the same reason it never did. RESIDUAL, honest and narrow: the bare zero-argument invocation is still ungatable here — no boundary trick distinguishes it from the project name standing alone — and a first-level verb not yet in the alternation is not matched. A THIRD residual is structural and worth naming precisely, because needle (6) closes only part of it — note that path-QUALIFIED invocations are NOT in this residual set: the guard's path arm covers them on every signature that carries the guard, which is what the previous separate-needle design failed to do for the flag-first and continuation forms. no single-line matcher can see a multi-line construct, so a continuation written WITHOUT a backslash (inside a YAML block scalar, an array of argv strings, a prose sentence wrapping between executable and verb) is invisible to every needle here. Closing that class needs a line-joining pre-pass in path-canonical-ripple.ts, not another needle — the same shape as the wrap-split cite residual recorded on failure-mode-catalog.md CAT-06. All three stay audit-layer, recorded on CAT-01 Known Gaps as well as here. SCOPE includes the ROOT package.json plus apps/**/package.json and packages/**/package.json so the bin-map needles gate the SHIPPED manifest (apps/cli/package.json, authored by Plan-007 T-007r-3-1) and not only documentation examples; that file does not exist yet, and git grep simply finds nothing until it does. The root manifest is listed as its own glob because neither `apps/**` nor `packages/**` reaches it, and it is not merely a manifest: a workspace-root script (`"daemon:status": "sidekicks daemon status"`) is a runnable invocation that the verb needle must gate. Including it costs nothing, because the root manifest's own `"name": "ai-sidekicks"` is a VALUE and needle (3) is key-position-anchored against exactly that. SCOPE also covers implementation sources (apps/**/src/**/*.ts, *.tsx, apps/**/*.html, packages/**/src/**/*.ts) so the gate protects runtime surfaces, not only manifests and prose — the `sidekicks://` protocol handler Plan-023 registers under apps/desktop/src/main/, the renderer HTML that carries the same scheme, and the future apps/cli/src/ entry point and its help output. All six needles were verified to return zero across that scope, each proven to match BOTH the bare and the path-qualified spelling of its signature where one exists, and each was proven to MATCH its intended form on a planted probe rather than assumed to. docs/reference/** is excluded because that excerpted-upstream tree uses `ai-sidekicks` as the PROJECT name in prose and legitimately contains a project-name-plus-verb sequence (design-audits/runtime-execution.md, discussing this system's run state machine); docs/archive/** and docs/superpowers/** are dated-provenance trees. docs/operations/failure-mode-catalog.md is deliberately NOT excluded from this entry, unlike entry 1: that exclusion exists there because the catalog must spell entry 1's deprecated path literally to document the pattern, whereas this canonicalization is written up on CAT-01 without spelling any dead form, and the catalog is a live operations document a regression could land in. SLASH EXCEPTION: needle (5) is the one deprecated form ending in a slash. The trailing `//` is the URL-scheme delimiter, not a directory slash, and it is load-bearing against a false positive — `ai-sidekicks:` alone would match the unchanged keystore key prefix. A URL scheme has no CLI/executable form, so the blind spot the no-slash rule guards does not exist here; the allowlist exception lives in tools/docs-corpus/__tests__/path-canonical-ripple.test.ts per that test's own instruction.

Second entry for the same canonical, split out ONLY to carry a narrower scope. The call form `setAsDefaultProtocolClient('ai-sidekicks')` — the Electron deep-link registration Plan-023 pins under apps/desktop/src/main/ — carries no `://`, so the scheme needle on the main entry cannot see it. It cannot live on that entry either, because a backticked project name inside parentheses is legitimate, common prose in the doc corpus (Plan-007's own Decision Log writes one), and that entry scopes docs/**/*.md; here the scope is implementation sources only, where a bare project name as a lone call argument has no legitimate meaning. MATCHER: regex, so ONE needle covers all three string-literal delimiters (single, double, backtick) plus argument-position whitespace, instead of one fixed-string needle per spelling — the treadmill three successive review rounds walked before this. The needle is ANCHORED ON THE FUNCTION NAME, not on the argument alone. Without that guard it would match any single-argument call whose value is the deliberately-unchanged project name — an `expect(packageName).toBe("ai-sidekicks")` assertion in a test, a workspace helper — and this entry's scope is every application and package source file, so such a call is ordinary, legitimate code. Narrowing to the function name rather than narrowing the scope to one file keeps the gate useful if the registration ever moves, while removing the false-positive class entirely. Verified zero across this scope, proven to match all three delimiter spellings on planted probes, and proven NOT to match the legitimate `pnpm --filter 'ai-sidekicks'` shell form, which has no enclosing parentheses. HONEST LIMIT, deliberately not chased further: a regex over source text still cannot enumerate string-literal CONSTRUCTS. String.raw, concatenation, a variable, or a computed name would each escape. This is best-effort coverage of the constructs the pinned design has today; when apps/cli/ and the Electron protocol registration actually land, the real guard is code review plus a typed constant for the scheme, not this registry.
